concepts.title: 1. Class Marks and Direct Method
concepts.subtitle: Midpoints as weighted representatives
concepts.summary: Each class interval is represented by its class mark, the midpoint of the interval. The Direct Method uses frequencies as weights to calculate the mean.
concepts.trap: Using a class limit or class width instead of the midpoint.

concepts.title: 2. Assumed Mean Method
concepts.subtitle: Deviations simplify arithmetic
concepts.summary: Choose a convenient assumed mean a, calculate d_i=x_i-a, form f_i d_i, and use the correction formula.
concepts.trap: Reversing the deviation sign without changing the correction formula.

concepts.title: 3. One Missing Frequency
concepts.subtitle: Mean condition gives one equation
concepts.summary: Put the unknown frequency in both total frequency and weighted total, then use the given mean to form a linear equation.
concepts.trap: Putting the unknown frequency in only one part of the mean.

concepts.title: 4. Two Missing Frequencies
concepts.subtitle: Two conditions, two unknowns
concepts.summary: Use total frequency for one equation and the mean condition for the second, then solve simultaneously.

points.text: Use $\sum f_ix_i=\bar xN$ for the second equation.

concepts.trap: Trying to determine two frequencies from only one condition.
